strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing practical challenges in automated visual prompt discovery for LVLMs, with clear motivation and positioning

Solid technical framework that thoughtfully decouples semantic intent from implementation, reducing cognitive load on exploration and enabling efficient search in high-level idea space rather than low-level code
Strong empirical results: achieves 78.9% average accuracy vs. 64.6% for SketchPad, with 91.2% reduction in inference tokens and only 11.5% of baseline exploration cost
Important empirical finding on non-transferability of visual prompts across LVLM architectures (Table 4), which justifies automated model-specific discovery
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with ablation studies, multiple metrics (accuracy, inference efficiency, exploration efficiency, stability), and qualitative analysis of discovered prompts
Outperforms baselines on 7 of 9 tasks with particularly strong gains on BlindTest benchmark, demonstrating effectiveness of semantic exploration approach
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: NUCT is a straightforward adaptation of existing UCB/UCT algorithms; semantic backpropagation is primarily LLM-based summarization without substantial technical innovation

Heavy reliance on LLM capabilities with insufficient validation: success depends critically on quality of Gemini's idea generation and self-evaluation; reliability of heuristic scores (s_gain, s_novel) not validated; creates problematic meta-dependency (using LLMs to improve LVLMs)

Narrow evaluation scope limiting generalizability: only 9 tasks focusing on geometric/spatial perception, primarily tested on single LVLM (Gemini-2.5-flash), unclear extension to other perception failure types or model architectures
Small development set (30 images per task) with high overfitting risk; while stability is reported, generalization analysis is limited and representative power of small dev set unclear

Insufficient ablation and sensitivity analysis: hyperparameters appear ad-hoc (λ_expl=0.5, λ_novel=0.15, λ_sat=0.5, k=3) without justification; ablations limited to 2 tasks; no sensitivity studies for iteration count or other design choices

Limited theoretical grounding: no convergence analysis or exploration bounds for NUCT; why semantic space is superior to code space not rigorously justified; non-transferability phenomenon not deeply mechanistically analyzed

Reproducibility concerns: depends on closed-source Gemini-2.5-flash; complex system with many carefully-tuned LLM prompts; solution space constrained by pre-defined tool set; asymmetry in thinking feature during exploration vs. inference

Incomplete failure analysis: only 2 tasks where SEVEX underperforms with minimal analysis; missing systematic investigation of when and why the approach fails or what types of prompts it cannot discover

Scalability questions: each task/model combination requires independent exploration; upfront cost high (3,442 naive inferences) though amortized; unclear how approach scales to diverse, real-world visual reasoning tasks beyond the narrow benchmark sets

strengths: Well-motivated problem with novel framing: operating in abstract idea space rather than raw code to avoid low-level distraction and unstructured search
Thoughtful technical design combining idea-implementation decoupling, novelty-guided tree search, and semantic backpropagation for learning
Comprehensive empirical evaluation across two benchmarks with multiple metrics (accuracy, inference cost, exploration efficiency) and clear baselines
Strong experimental results: 78.9% average accuracy vs 71.6% Naive and 64.6% SketchPad, with 91.2% reduction in inference tokens
Discovery of non-obvious counter-intuitive strategies (Jigsaw depth estimation example) demonstrating genuine novelty beyond conventional tool usage
Important analysis of visual prompt non-transferability across models, providing strong motivation for automated discovery
Excellent reproducibility with comprehensive prompts, hyperparameters, and implementation details in appendices
Ablation studies validate all major components (tree structure, semantic backpropagation, abstract space) contribute meaningfully
weaknesses: Limited evaluation scope: only one primary LVLM (Gemini-2.5-flash) with cross-model validation on just 1 task; only 9 tasks on specialized benchmarks; unclear generalization to broader visual reasoning tasks

Computational costs not fully transparent: exploration cost expressed as relative counts not absolute tokens/time; no analysis of cost scaling; asymmetric setup (thinking disabled for baselines but enabled for SEVEX)

Insufficient analysis of LLM dependency: entire framework relies on agent capabilities for idea generation/implementation/analysis; no sensitivity analysis for LLM choice or prompt engineering; no validation of semantic backpropagation insight quality

Limited algorithmic novelty: NUCT is primarily UCB with novelty scoring (incremental combination); lacks theoretical justification for design choices (why R_i^max vs mean reward in Eq. 1, specific saturation term formulation, hyperparameter sensitivity)

Baseline comparison concerns: SketchPad+APE applies text-based optimization to programmatic prompts (questionable adaptation); missing simpler baselines (random search, genetic algorithms); SketchPad modified with added tools

Semantic backpropagation rigor: complex information flow through tree not clearly specified; unclear how conflicting insights from different children resolve; backpropagation to all ancestors may lack specificity; limited ablation (only 2 tasks)

Generalization questions inadequately addressed: despite non-transferability motivation, framework still requires per-model discovery; no analysis of performance variation across task types; development set size effects not explored; tool set dependency not discussed

Technical presentation issues: dense Figure 2 hard to parse; notation inconsistencies; tree termination conditions not specified; unclear how child nodes expand/prune; NUCT formula uses unexplained notation at initialization

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear practical value; non-transferability finding (Section 4.6) is important and well-documented
Comprehensive experimental validation across 9 tasks and 3 LVLM backbones, with superior accuracy (78.9% vs. 64.6-71.6% baselines) and excellent inference efficiency
Coherent technical approach combining semantic exploration, novelty-guided UCT, and sample-wise analysis through semantic backpropagation
Discovery of counter-intuitive visual strategies (e.g., depth estimation for naturalness detection in Jigsaw) demonstrates capability to escape human bias
Thorough ablations (Figure 5), sensitivity analysis (Appendix C.2), and restricted-toolbox validation (C.1) strengthen claims about generalization
Clear presentation with effective figures; comprehensive appendix with implementation details and prompts
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty in individual components: NUCT is incremental UCT extension, semantic backpropagation is LLM-based analysis, idea generation entirely LLM-driven; innovation is primarily in orchestration

Circular dependence on LLM reasoning capabilities; framework success depends on LLM's ability to generate/evaluate ideas, yet this is never validated. Unfair experimental setup: 'thinking' feature disabled for baselines but enabled for SEVEX, biasing results
Small development sets (30 images) with generalization validated only on CircledLetter; risk of overfitting across remaining 8 tasks unaddressed. No analysis of scaling with development set size

Non-transferability severely limits practical impact: requires expensive discovery for each model, incompatible with rapidly-evolving LVLM landscape, suggests discovered prompts are brittle model-specific artifacts rather than robust strategies

Narrow evaluation scope: only 9 tasks with discrete correctness metrics, mostly synthetic (BlindTest uses pure geometry). Unclear generalization to open-ended visual reasoning, semantic tasks, or real-world scenarios

Weak baseline comparisons: SketchPad's 47.4% surprisingly low; SketchPad+APE shows large dev-test gap (51.7%→38.9%) suggesting underperformance. No comparison to simpler alternatives (random search, Bayesian optimization, genetic algorithms)

Insufficient analysis of search dynamics: tree growth properties unclear, hyperparameter sensitivity (λ^expl, λ^novel, λ^sat, k) not studied, self-evaluation reliability unvalidated, feasibility prediction accuracy not assessed

Cost-benefit analysis incomplete: breakeven at 273 inferences assumes prompt reuse; doesn't address frequent model updates, task distribution shifts, or scenarios with fewer inferences. Real-world applicability in production unclear
Reproducibility concerns: relies on proprietary models (Gemini, GPT-4o, Claude) and external tools, no code/data availability mentioned, random seeds and API configurations incompletely specified

Limited theoretical understanding: no regret analysis for NUCT, no validation that s^gain/s^novel correlate with performance, no analysis of which idea types are most effective, no failure case discussion

strengths: Novel and well-motivated framework addressing a real limitation of LVLMs: systematic perception failures despite strong reasoning capabilities. The finding about non-transferability of visual prompts across models is particularly valuable.

Strong empirical results across multiple dimensions: 78.9% average accuracy (vs 71.6% naive, 64.6% SketchPad), 11.5% of competitor's exploration cost, and only 10.9% inference cost increase over baseline. Consistent improvements across three different LVLM backbones.

Thoughtful system design with the abstract idea space approach elegantly addressing the long-context distraction problem inherent in raw code search. Semantic backpropagation that extracts actionable insights from sample-wise analysis is a nice design element.

Comprehensive experimental validation including appropriate baselines, component ablations (Figure 5), restricted-toolbox sensitivity analysis, and cross-backbone generalization. Stability analysis across development splits provides evidence against overfitting.

Qualitative analysis reveals counter-intuitive discovered solutions (e.g., using depth estimation creatively in Jigsaw task), demonstrating the framework discovers effective strategies beyond human expectations and conventional tool usage.
Clear presentation with effective visualizations; the paper is well-written and the core ideas are accessible. Problem formulation and motivation are compelling.
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: NUCT is a straightforward adaptation of standard UCB/UCT; semantic backpropagation is essentially LLM-based analysis. The contribution is more systems/engineering-focused than advancing fundamental techniques. No theoretical analysis of convergence or optimality properties provided.

Fairness concerns in baseline comparisons: (1) Thinking feature enabled for SEVEX discovery but disabled for baseline inference, providing unfair advantage; (2) SketchPad modified with drawing tools it wasn't designed for; (3) Different computational budgets/nature of iterations across baselines unclear.

Limited evaluation scope: Only 9 tasks, all specialized geometric/spatial perception. No evaluation on broader LVLM failure modes (semantic understanding, hallucination, etc.). Generalization beyond these specific perception tasks remains unclear.

Hyperparameter selection not justified: λ values and k=3 appear arbitrary with no sensitivity analysis. 50 iterations lacks principled justification. Unclear if hyperparameters should be tuned per-task, limiting practical applicability.

Incomplete scalability and generality analysis: What when suitable tools unavailable? How does performance scale to larger strategy spaces? 30-image dev set quite small. Model-specific discovery requirement limits practical deployment.

Statistical rigor lacking: No confidence intervals or significance tests for main results. Standard deviations only for CircledLetter. Some tasks show modest improvements (OverlappingShapes: 50.4%→52.4%). Incomplete cost analysis mixing token and algorithmic costs.

Failure analysis insufficient: Limited discussion of underperformance cases (e.g., Claude CircledLetter: 90.7% SketchPad vs 80.5% SEVEX). Restricted toolbox sometimes outperforms full system. Root causes of unsuccessful iterations not explored.

Reproducibility concerns: No code release mentioned; heavy dependence on Gemini-2.5-flash's specific behavior which may drift. Agent prompt engineering choices not fully transparent despite appendix. Idea space constraints and feasibility checks insufficiently specified.
